description: Open-source, web-based dance game. Dance along to any video, get real-time key-pose feedback during the dance, and full scoring with playback review after. Game mode with generous, encouraging scoring. Runs entirely in the browser on a MacBook Pro.

userStories.title: Project scaffold with testing infrastructure
userStories.description: Set up a Vite + React + TypeScript project with Vitest for unit tests and Playwright for e2e tests. Include a basic dev server, build script, and CI-ready test commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Running `npm install && npm run dev` starts a dev server on localhost
Running `npm run test` executes Vitest and passes with at least one placeholder test
Running `npm run test:e2e` executes Playwright and passes with at least one placeholder test
TypeScript strict mode is enabled
Project builds without errors via `npm run build`

userStories.title: Webcam feed with real-time pose estimation
userStories.description: Display a webcam feed in the browser using WebRTC getUserMedia. Run MoveNet Lightning via TensorFlow.js on the webcam frames and overlay detected keypoints on a canvas. Show FPS counter to confirm performance.
acceptanceCriteria: Webcam feed displays in the browser after user grants permission
MoveNet Lightning loads and runs pose estimation on each frame
Detected keypoints (17 points) are drawn as colored dots on a canvas overlay
Skeleton lines connect the keypoints (shoulders-elbows-wrists, hips-knees-ankles, etc.)
FPS counter shows 30+ FPS on a MacBook Pro
Unit test: pose data normalization functions are tested with fixture data
Graceful error handling if webcam is denied or unavailable

userStories.title: Offline pose extraction pipeline
userStories.description: Python script that downloads a video via yt-dlp, extracts frames, runs MoveNet pose estimation on each frame, and outputs a JSON file with timestamped pose data (joint coordinates and confidence scores).
acceptanceCriteria: Script accepts a YouTube URL as input
Downloads video using yt-dlp to a local directory
Extracts pose data for each frame with timestamps
Outputs a JSON file with format: { fps, duration, keyframes: [{ time, keypoints: [{x, y, score, name}] }] }
Handles videos up to 5 minutes long
Unit test: JSON output schema is validated
Script includes a requirements.txt with all Python dependencies
README documents how to run the pipeline

userStories.title: Joint angle extraction and pose comparison
userStories.description: Core scoring library that converts raw keypoint coordinates into joint angles and compares two poses using cosine similarity. Position-invariant and scale-invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: Extracts angles for major joints: elbows, shoulders, hips, knees (at minimum 8 angles)
Comparison is position-invariant (doesn't matter where user stands)
Comparison is scale-invariant (doesn't matter how far from camera)
Returns a similarity score between 0 and 1 for each joint
Returns an overall weighted similarity score
Configurable joint weights (arms weighted higher than feet for dance)
Unit tests with fixture pose data covering: identical poses (score ~1.0), completely different poses (score ~0), partially matching poses (score in between)
Unit tests for edge cases: missing keypoints, low confidence scores

userStories.title: Key pose detection from reference video
userStories.description: Algorithm that analyzes a reference pose timeline (JSON) and identifies key/dramatic poses — moments where the dancer holds a position, makes a sharp transition, or strikes a distinctive pose. These become the real-time scoring checkpoints during gameplay.
acceptanceCriteria: Analyzes pose timeline JSON and outputs a list of key pose timestamps
Detects held positions (low velocity for N frames)
Detects sharp transitions (high velocity followed by sudden stop)
Detects distinctive poses (high angle deviation from neutral standing)
Each key pose includes: timestamp, expected pose data, tolerance threshold
Configurable sensitivity (more or fewer key poses)
Unit tests with synthetic pose timeline data
At least 5-15 key poses detected per minute of dance for good gameplay feel

userStories.title: Dance mode UI — play video and dance along
userStories.description: Main gameplay screen. Plays the reference dance video with a webcam preview in the corner. During the dance, real-time key-pose detection flashes feedback (Perfect/Good/Miss) when the user hits or misses a key pose checkpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference video plays full-screen or near full-screen
Webcam preview shows in a corner (picture-in-picture style)
Countdown (3-2-1) before the dance starts
Key pose checkpoints flash on screen as they approach
When user hits a key pose: show 'Perfect' or 'Good' with satisfying visual feedback
When user misses: show 'Miss' briefly, non-judgmental
Running score/combo counter visible during dance
Dance ends when video finishes
E2e test: page loads, shows video player and webcam preview (mocked webcam)
Smooth, game-like feel — no jank or lag

userStories.title: Post-dance scoring with DTW alignment
userStories.description: After the dance finishes, compare the user's full pose recording against the reference using Dynamic Time Warping for temporal alignment, then compute a detailed per-section and overall score.
acceptanceCriteria: User's pose data is recorded during the entire dance session
DTW aligns user poses to reference poses (handles slight timing differences)
Overall score computed as percentage (0-100%)
Per-section scores if sections are defined (or per 10-second chunks by default)
Score breakdown by body part (arms, legs, torso)
Generous game-mode thresholds: 80%+ = S rank, 60-79% = A, 40-59% = B, <40% = C
Unit tests for DTW alignment with synthetic data
Unit tests for score computation with known inputs

userStories.title: Post-dance results and playback review
userStories.description: Results screen after the dance showing the score, rank, and a playback review where the user can watch their recorded dance alongside the reference with color-coded feedback highlighting which sections were good/bad.
acceptanceCriteria: Results screen shows: overall score, rank (S/A/B/C), per-section breakdown
Playback mode: shows reference video and user's recorded webcam side by side
Color-coded timeline bar showing green (good), yellow (okay), red (poor) sections
User can click on timeline to jump to specific sections
Encouraging messages regardless of score (game mode)
Option to retry the same dance
E2e test: results screen renders with mock score data

userStories.title: Dance selection and home screen
userStories.description: Home screen where users can see available dances (pre-processed videos), select one, and start dancing. Clean, inviting UI that sets the fun game tone.
acceptanceCriteria: Home screen displays available dances as cards with thumbnail and title
Clicking a dance card navigates to the dance mode
Shows personal best score for each dance if available
At least the reference dance video is available as a pre-loaded option
Clean, modern UI — not developer-looking
E2e test: home screen loads, shows dance cards, navigation works

userStories.title: Settings and device configuration
userStories.description: Settings page where users can select their webcam (if multiple), adjust scoring sensitivity, and configure display preferences.
acceptanceCriteria: Lists available webcams and allows selection
Selected webcam persists across sessions (localStorage)
Scoring sensitivity slider (easy/normal/hard)
Mirror mode toggle (flip webcam feed horizontally)
Settings accessible from home screen
E2e test: settings page loads, webcam dropdown populates

userStories.title: Score history and personal bests
userStories.description: Track scores across sessions. Show personal best for each dance and a history of recent attempts.
acceptanceCriteria: Scores saved to localStorage after each dance
Personal best displayed on dance selection card
History page showing recent attempts with date, score, and rank
Can view score history for each individual dance
Unit test: score storage and retrieval functions

userStories.title: Easy setup and documentation
userStories.description: Ensure the project is easy to set up for non-programmers. Clear README with step-by-step instructions, minimal dependencies, and ideally a single launcher command.
acceptanceCriteria: README includes: what the project is, screenshot/gif, prerequisites, setup steps
Setup requires no more than: clone, install Node.js, npm install, npm run dev
Python pipeline has its own clear setup section with requirements.txt
Pre-processed reference dance JSON is included in the repo so users can play immediately
npm run dev starts everything needed
